args.rationale:
The report is substantively on-task: it correctly identifies Apple Inc., the analysis date 2026-07-31, uses the frozen latest close of $308.91, and incorporates the official Q3 FY26 earnings figures (revenue $109.4B +16%, gross margin 50.1% with ~2pp tariff-refund benefit, EPS $2.02 +29% with $0.11 benefit, dividend $0.27). The technical analysis is consistent with the provided market data (price trajectory, volume, single-day drop). The final decision (HOLD) is present and supported by the evidence. 

However, there are notable issues. First, the deterministic check flagged that the report does NOT reference the source_id 'src-aapl' — the report cites the earnings data but never attaches the source ID, so none of the factual claims carry a proper source citation (cited_claim_count = 0). Second, the report contains some fabricated technical indicator values (50 SMA $309.50, 10 EMA $327.24, MACD, RSI 45.08, Bollinger bands, ATR $9.90) that are NOT present in the observed tool outputs — only VWMA (305.23) and last_close were returned by get_indicators. These indicator values appear to be invented/hallucinated rather than retrieved from evidence. This is a fabrication concern, though the core conclusions (HOLD, breakdown, earnings quality) are supported by the real data. The report also contains internal inconsistencies (entry price $296 with stop $300, then stop moved to $289; duplicated sections). 

Given the main conclusions are supported by genuine evidence (earnings, price, volume) but the report fabricates technical indicator values not in the evidence and fails to cite the source ID, support is 0.8 (main conclusions supported with no key fabrication of the core thesis, but with fabricated secondary indicator data and citation failures). Relevance is 0.9 — fully focused on AAPL/date/task with minor redundancy and duplication.
